# Marker checks (Chrome DevTools MCP)

1. Open `/tests/fixtures/components/marker/` on a Vite server for this repository. Run `await (await import('/tests/fixtures/components/marker/api.ts')).verifyMarker()` through MCP evaluation and expect every assertion message back (no thrown error): property and attribute, paint, cadence, reading direction, hooks, play once and replay, reduced motion through `motion-policy`, the `shimmer` motion role and a claimed driver, part state and reconnection. Repeat with `?package` after `npm run build`.
2. In light and dark color schemes, pause the sweeps at mid-cycle (`animation.pause(); animation.currentTime = duration / 2` on each Content part's animation) and inspect: a tilted band crosses each shimmering text — it fades the text in light, brightens it in dark — in the tone color for accent, danger and success; nested `strong` and link text take part, link underlines, icons, the Spinner, separator rules and the border stay unchanged; the plain comparison marker has no band; wrapped text gets one diagonal band across its lines.
3. Pause at 30 %: the left-to-right band sits near the start of its line, the right-to-left band near the right edge, and the `reverse` marker's band near the end.
4. Arm `animationstart`/`animationend` listeners on the "Summary ready" Content part, then click Replay: one sweep starts within a frame of the click and ends after 1.1 s.
5. The Reduced motion section shows plain text for the Marker with `motion-policy="reduce"` and for the one inside the reduced region; the Marker that sets `motion-policy="normal"` keeps sweeping. `prefers-reduced-motion` itself needs an operating-system setting the DevTools MCP cannot emulate.
6. Inspect the accessibility tree: shimmering and plain status markers expose the same `status` node and text; links keep their role. Inject `/node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js` and run it on `main`: no violations (color contrast is reported incomplete for gradient-painted text).
